recipes.title: Stuffed Lamb Saddle with Roasted Baby Vegetables and Israeli Couscous

ingredients.name: boneless lamb saddle, butterflied and trimmed
baby carrots, zucchini, and baby turnips, trimmed
crumbled feta cheese or pine nut herb stuffing
fresh rosemary and thyme, finely chopped
lamb or vegetable stock for aromatic jus

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Season butterflied lamb saddle generously inside and out with salt, pepper, garlic, and fresh herbs.
Spread chopped spinach and crumbled feta (or pine nut herb stuffing) evenly over the interior surface of the meat.
Roll the saddle tightly into a neat cylinder and secure at 1-inch intervals with butcher's twine.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in an oven-safe skillet or roasting pan over medium-high heat. Sear the tied saddle on all sides for 4-5 minutes until rich golden-brown.
Scatter baby vegetables around the saddle, drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil, and transfer to oven to roast for 35 to 45 minutes until internal thermometer reads 135°F-140°F for medium-rare.
Cook Israeli couscous in boiling salted water or stock for 8-10 minutes until tender; drain and toss with fresh herbs.
Transfer rested roasted lamb to a board and tent loosely with foil for 10 minutes. Deglaze roasting pan with 1 cup stock to create aromatic pan jus.
Remove twine, carve lamb saddle into thick medallions, and serve over warm Israeli couscous with roasted baby vegetables and warm jus.
recipes.swaps: Goat cheese or sun-dried tomato tapenade can replace feta; quinoa can replace Israeli couscous.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Butcher's twine, heavy roasting pan, meat thermometer. Premium showstopper presentation.

recipes.title: Lamb Shoulder with Herbs de Provence

ingredients.name: Herbes de Provence (thyme, rosemary, oregano, marjoram, savory)
dry white wine or chicken broth
baby red or Yukon gold potatoes, halved

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C). Pat lamb shoulder completely dry.
Make small incisions all over the lamb with a paring knife and insert garlic slivers deep into the meat.
Rub the entire lamb shoulder with olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper, and generous coatings of Herbes de Provence.
Place seasoned lamb shoulder in a heavy Dutch oven or roasting pan. Arrange halved baby potatoes and carrot chunks around the meat.
Pour white wine or broth into the bottom of the pan without washing spices off the meat.
Cover tightly with lid or a double layer of heavy-duty foil. Braise in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until fork-tender and collagen has melted.
Remove lid, increase oven temperature to 400°F (200°C), and roast for 15-20 minutes until a deeply caramelized crust develops.
Rest for 15 minutes before pulling the succulent meat apart with two forks and serving with braised potatoes and pan juices.
recipes.swaps: Can substitute red wine for white wine; sweet potatoes can replace red potatoes.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Large Dutch oven with tight lid. Slow braising breaks down connective tissue in collagen-rich shoulder.

recipes.title: Classic Roast Lamb Leg with Gravy

ingredients.name: fresh rosemary, picked into small clusters
beef or lamb broth (for pan gravy)
roasting potatoes (floury variety like Russet or Sebago), cut into chunks

steps: Preheat oven to 390°F (200°C) / 350°F fan.
Cut deep slits all over the lamb leg using a small knife. Push slivers of garlic and rosemary clusters deep into the cuts.
Rub the leg thoroughly with olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Place lamb on a wire rack inside a roasting pan. Toss potato chunks in 1 tbsp oil, season with salt, and place around the base.
Roast for 15 minutes at 390°F, then turn oven down to 350°F (180°C) and roast for 1 hour 15 minutes for medium-rare (135°F-140°F internal).
Remove lamb and potatoes from oven. Transfer lamb to a platter, tent loosely with foil, and rest 15-20 minutes.

For gravy: Place roasting pan on stovetop over medium heat. Skim excess fat, leaving 2 tbsp. Sprinkle flour into pan drippings and whisk 1 minute. Pour in broth, scraping up browned bits, and simmer 3-4 minutes until rich and thickened.
Carve lamb leg into tender slices across the grain and serve with crispy roast potatoes and hot gravy.

source_temperatures.target: Pull at 135°F for medium-rare (carries over to 145°F rested)

recipes.swaps: Can use boneless leg of lamb (reduce roasting time by 15-20 minutes); mint sauce pairs traditionally.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Roasting pan with rack, whisk, carving knife. Resting allows juices to settle evenly.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Rosemary Garlic Lamb Shoulder

ingredients.name: bone-in lamb shoulder (skin-on or fat cap trimmed)

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C). Pat lamb shoulder dry.
Place halved garlic head and rosemary sprigs in the bottom of a deep roasting pan or Dutch oven. Pour stock into pan.
Rub lamb shoulder generously with olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Place lamb directly on top of the aromatics.
Cover tightly with two layers of heavy-duty aluminum foil, crimping edges firmly to seal in all steam.
Roast in the oven for 3.5 to 4 hours until the meat is ultra-tender and pulls apart easily with a spoon.
Carefully uncover pan, baste meat with rich pan juices, and arrange halved potatoes in the surrounding liquid.
Return pan to oven uncovered, increase temperature to 400°F (200°C), and roast for 20-25 minutes until the exterior is browned and crispy.
Rest 10 minutes. Shred the lamb directly in the pan and serve bathed in natural rosemary garlic juices alongside roasted potatoes.
recipes.swaps: Can be cooked in a slow cooker on low for 8-9 hours; dried herbs can replace fresh in equal amounts.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Deep roasting pan, heavy foil. Lamb shoulder contains rich marbling that stays succulent over long cooking.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Melting Lamb Leg
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Layer onion rounds, crushed garlic, and herbs across the bottom of a large roasting pan. Pour in stock and wine.
Rub olive oil, salt, and pepper generously all over the lamb leg. Set lamb directly on the bed of onions.
Cover tightly with foil, sealing completely so no moisture escapes.
Roast slowly for 4 hours. Check meat; it should be meltingly soft and tender.
Uncover foil, ladle pan juices over lamb, and increase oven to 425°F (220°C). Roast 15-20 minutes until skin is golden-crisp.
Transfer lamb to platter. Skim pan juices, press garlic/onions through sieve into sauce, and simmer 5 minutes for a luscious jus.
Carve or pull meat with forks and serve drizzled with pan jus over warm crusty bread or mashed potatoes.

source_temperatures.target: Tender to the bone, internal temperature 195°F-205°F

recipes.swaps: Can substitute broth with 1 tbsp lemon juice for wine; serve with warm pita or flatbread.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Large roasting pan with tight-fitting lid or double foil. Perfect make-ahead centerpiece.

recipes.title: Chargrilled Lamb Fillet Steaks with Herb Salad

ingredients.name: lamb fillet steaks (cut from leg of lamb, trimmed)
fresh oregano and rosemary, finely chopped
crumbled feta cheese and cherry tomatoes

steps: In a shallow dish, combine olive oil, minced garlic, chopped oregano, rosemary, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss lamb fillet steaks in the marinade until thoroughly coated. Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Preheat grill or cast-iron grill pan to high heat until smoking hot.
Place lamb fillet steaks on grill; sear for 3 to 4 minutes per side for tender medium-rare doneness (130°F-135°F).
Transfer steaks to a cutting board, tent with foil, and rest for 5 minutes.
Slice steaks thinly across the grain into tender strips.
Arrange fresh baby greens, cherry tomatoes, and crumbled feta on serving plates.
Top the salad with warm sliced chargrilled lamb fillet steaks and drizzle with light lemon-herb vinaigrette.
recipes.swaps: Can use outdoor charcoal grill or indoor ridged grill pan; goat cheese can replace feta.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Grill pan or outdoor barbecue, tongs, meat thermometer. Quick, lean, nutrient-dense meal.

recipes.title: Sous Vide Lamb Chops with Cast-Iron Butter Sear

ingredients.name: Colorado lamb loin T-bone chops (or lamb rib chops, 1-inch thick)
high smoke-point oil (avocado or canola oil)

steps: Set immersion circulator in a water bath and preheat to 118°F–120°F for rare/medium-rare doneness.
Season lamb loin chops generously with kosher salt and cracked black pepper.
Place chops in cooking bags (4 per bag) with 1 tbsp butter, crushed garlic, and rosemary sprigs.
Remove air using vacuum sealer or water displacement method, then seal bags tightly.
Submerge in water bath and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours.
Remove chops from bags and discard juices. CRITICAL TECHNIQUE: Thoroughly pat all sides of the lamb chops completely dry with paper towels (wet meat will steam and prevent crust formation).
Heat avocado oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Sear lamb chops for 45 to 60 seconds on the first side without moving.
Flip chops, drop remaining 2 tbsp butter and garlic/herbs into pan. Rapidly spoon foaming butter over chops for 45 seconds to create a deep golden crust.
Remove chops immediately to a warm board, rest for 3 minutes, and serve.
recipes.swaps: Can substitute lamb cutlets or rib chops; ghee or beef tallow can replace butter for high-heat basting.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Sous vide immersion circulator, vacuum bags, cast iron skillet, paper towels. Paper-towel drying is essential for proper crust.
